mechanism_narrative: A higher level of labor employment (PAYEMS) signals positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as it indicates a strong labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window for PAYEMS predicting 5-day SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% triggers negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as it indicates a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) signals a monetary tightening cycle that compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months AND CPIAUCSL > 2.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 3 months and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 5.0%), a rising housing starts (HOUST) signals positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as it indicates strong consumer demand for housing and related sectors, which boosts corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST rises > 0.5% in 1 month and UNRATE < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 110.0 signals negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as it indicates a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate profits and equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 110.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a strong economy with tightening monetary policy, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 1 month AND FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of consumer credit (RSAFS) signals positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns, as it indicates strong consumer spending and corporate credit demand, supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window for RSAFS predicting 5-day SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.0% triggers negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.
